mainTopic: Signs of the generation of משיח, the dangers of calculating his arrival, and the six-thousand-year timeline of the world
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of when משיח comes. רבי יצחק quotes רבי יוחנן: the generation of בן דוד will have few scholars, deep sorrow, and troubles that come one after another. A ברייתא lays out the seven-year cycle before משיח, and אביי answers רב יוסף's challenge by pointing out that the full signs, in order, never happened. Several תנאים (רבי יהודה, רבי נהוראי, רבי נחמיה) describe a generation with no shame, no respect, and no truth, and רבא tells the story of a town called קושטא where even one white lie brought death. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק in דברים that משיח comes only at a low point: informers, few students, poverty, or despair. רבי זירא warns against calculating the date, since משיח comes when no one expects him. The amud ends with teachings about the world's timeline: six thousand years, a period of ruin, and three eras of תוהו, תורה, and ימות המשיח.

steps.title: Finishing the verse behind the name בר נפלי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the פסוק from עמוס that shows why משיח is called בר נפלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: …the Tabernacle of David that is fallen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a פסוק that started on the previous page. It is the source for calling משיח 'בר נפלי', the son of the fallen one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הנופלת, 'the fallen one', sounds like נפלי. So the name בר נפלי is tied to משיח, who will raise up the fallen kingdom of דוד. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer about when משיח comes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tabernacle of David, meaning the kingdom of the house of דוד
A name for משיח, 'son of the fallen one'

phrases.english: the Tabernacle of David that is fallen.
phrases.notes: End of עמוס 9:11. The word נופלת sounds like נפלי, which is where the name בר נפלי comes from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the פסוק begun on the previous page, which explains the name בר נפלי.
steps.raayaObject: That משיח is called בר נפלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 9:11, 'I will raise up the Tabernacle of David that is fallen'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the generation of משיח is full of troubles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers with רבי יוחנן's teaching. Before משיח comes, תלמידי חכמים grow few, people suffer, and new decrees keep coming one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן says. In the generation when בן דוד comes, Torah scholars become few. The rest of the people's eyes wear out from sorrow and sighing. Many troubles and harsh decrees keep starting again, so that before the first one is over, the second one rushes in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers רב נחמן's question about when משיח comes. He describes the kind of generation it will be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives no date. Instead, it describes the condition of that generation: less Torah, deep sadness, and troubles that never stop. The point is that troubles will pile on without a break.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation in which משיח, the son of דוד, comes

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan says:
phrases.notes: רבי יצחק is answering רב נחמן, who asked on the previous page when בר נפלי comes.

phrases.english: The generation in which the son of David comes,
Torah scholars become fewer,
and as for the rest, their eyes wear out with sorrow and sighing,
and many troubles and harsh decrees keep starting anew,
so that before the first one is over,
the second one hurries to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the name בר נפלי is explained, רבי יצחק answers the original question about when he comes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משיח comes in a generation with few scholars, great sorrow, and constant new troubles and decrees.

steps.title: The seven-year cycle in which משיח comes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what happens in each year of the שמיטה cycle in which בן דוד comes. It moves through uneven rain, famine, plenty, voices and wars, and משיח comes right after the seventh year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught about the seven-year cycle in which בן דוד comes. In the first year, the פסוק 'I will make it rain on one city and not on another' comes true. In the second, arrows of hunger are sent out. In the third, there is a great famine. Men, women, children, pious people and people of good deeds die, and Torah is forgotten by those who learn it. In the fourth, there is food but not enough. In the fifth, there is great plenty: people eat, drink and rejoice, and Torah comes back to those who learn it. In the sixth, voices. In the seventh, wars. Right after the seventh, בן דוד comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out a year-by-year timeline of the seven years before משיח comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן described the generation in general, but this ברייתא gives a detailed order of events within one שמיטה cycle. Hunger grows from partial to great, then turns into plenty, and Torah is lost and then returns. The cycle ends with voices and wars, and משיח arrives in the year after the seventh.

keyTerms.meaning: A seven-year cycle, the שמיטה cycle
Arrows of famine, hunger striking here and there
The time right after the seventh year ends

steps.whyThisMatters: This timeline is what רב יוסף challenges in the next step. Its exact order becomes the key to אביי's answer.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁבוּעַ שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד בָּא בּוֹ,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the seven-year cycle in which the son of David comes:
phrases.notes: שבוע here means a seven-year שמיטה cycle, not a week.

phrases.english: in the first year, this verse is fulfilled:
"And I will cause it to rain upon one city
and upon another city I will not cause it to rain."
phrases.notes: עמוס 4:7

phrases.english: In the second year, arrows of famine are sent out.
In the third year, a great famine,
and men, women and children die,
pious people and people of good deeds,
and the Torah is forgotten by those who learn it.
In the fourth year, plenty, but not full plenty.
In the fifth year, great plenty,
and they eat, drink and rejoice,
and the Torah returns to those who learn it.
In the sixth year, voices.
In the seventh year, wars.
After the seventh year ends, the son of David comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁבוּעַ שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד בָּא בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detailed year-by-year timeline to רבי יוחנן's general description.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the שמיטה cycle before משיח, the years bring, in order: uneven rain, scattered famine, great famine, partial plenty, great plenty, voices, and wars. בן דוד comes right after the seventh year.

steps.title: רב יוסף: we have already seen such cycles
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the ברייתא. Many seven-year cycles have already looked like this, yet משיח did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Look, there have been many seven-year cycles that were like this, and he did not come!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the ברייתא using real-life experience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If these signs mean משיח is coming, then cycles with famine and plenty should have brought him. Since they did not, the ברייתא's signs seem unreliable.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא כַּמָּה שָׁבוּעֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Look, how many seven-year cycles there have been
that were like this, and he did not come!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא כַּמָּה שָׁבוּעֵי דַּהֲוָה כֵּן, וְלָא אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the timeline of the ברייתא in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's list of signs for the seven-year cycle before משיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cycles matching this description have already happened without משיח coming, so the signs seem not to predict his arrival.

steps.title: אביי: the full signs, in order, never happened
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the voices of the sixth year and the wars of the seventh have never happened. The signs have also never come in the exact order the ברייתא lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the sixth year voices, in the seventh year wars: did that ever happen? And besides, did all these things ever happen in their proper order?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא and answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי makes two points. First, famines and good years have happened, but the last two signs, voices and wars, never did. Second, even the signs that did happen never came in the exact order. So no past cycle truly matched the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Did it happen? (a question that expects 'no')

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's signs only count if all of them happen, including the voices and wars, and in the exact order listed.

phrases.english: Abaye said: In the sixth year, voices,
in the seventh year, wars: did that ever happen?
And furthermore, did they ever happen in their order?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּשִׁשִּׁית קוֹלוֹת, בִּשְׁבִיעִית מִלְחָמוֹת – מִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the condition: the full set of signs, in order, has never happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any cycle with famine and plenty fits the ברייתא, so משיח should have come.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a cycle with all the signs, including voices and wars, in the right order, matches the ברייתא, and that has never happened.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the shameful state of the generation of משיח
steps.stepSummary: After quoting the פסוק about 'the footsteps of Your anointed', the גמרא brings רבי יהודה's ברייתא. It describes the generation before משיח: Torah halls turned to sin, regions destroyed, refugees ignored, wisdom rotting, God-fearing people despised, and a brazen generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That Your enemies have taunted, ה׳, that they have taunted the footsteps of Your anointed.' It was taught: רבי יהודה says, in the generation when בן דוד comes, the meeting hall of the Sages will become a place of immorality. The Galilee will be destroyed, and the Gavlan will be laid waste. The people of the border will wander from city to city and no one will pity them. The wisdom of the scholars will rot, people who fear sin will be hated, and the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the 'footsteps of משיח', the time just before he comes. Then it brings רבי יהודה's ברייתא describing that generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps spoke about troubles, famines and wars. רבי יהודה adds moral and spiritual collapse: holy places misused, Torah wisdom spoiled, and good people looked down on. The 'face of a dog' shows a generation without shame.

keyTerms.meaning: The footsteps of Your anointed, the time just before משיח
The meeting hall where the Sages gathered

phrases.english: "That Your enemies have taunted, Lord,
that they have taunted the footsteps of Your anointed."
phrases.notes: תהלים 89:52

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
the generation in which the son of David comes:
the meeting hall will become a place of immorality,
and the Galilee will be destroyed,
and the Gavlan will be laid waste,
phrases.notes: Gavlan is a region, and יאשם here means 'will be desolate,' not 'guilty.'

phrases.english: and the people of the border will wander from city to city
and will not be shown pity,
and the wisdom of the scholars will rot,
and those who fear sin will be despised,
and the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דּוֹר שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד בָּא בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the seven-year timeline to a new teaching about the 'footsteps of משיח', describing that generation's moral state.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation of משיח will be marked by misused holy places, destroyed regions, unpitied refugees, spoiled wisdom, despised God-fearing people, and shameless faces.

steps.title: The last sign: truth will be missing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ברייתא ends with the sign that truth will be missing, and it brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And truth will be missing.' As the פסוק says: 'And truth is missing, and whoever turns away from evil is made a fool of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה from Step 6 finishes its list with one more sign: truth will be missing. It supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the final item in רבי יהודה's list, so it is not a new teaching. The ברייתא shows that this sign is already written in ישעיהו. The next steps explain both halves of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a fool of, treated as crazy

phrases.english: 'And the truth will be missing,'
as it is stated: 'And the truth is missing,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 59:15

phrases.english: and he who turns away from evil is made a fool of.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of signs in רבי יהודה's ברייתא from Step 6 and gives its source in a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before משיח, truth will be missing, as ישעיהו 59:15 says.

steps.title: What does 'truth is missing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the first half of the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and the truth is missing' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words 'truth is missing' mean. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Truth cannot simply vanish, so the גמרא wants to know what the word נעדרת is describing. The answer will be built on a play on that word.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'And the truth is missing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the first half of the פסוק quoted in Step 7 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word נעדרת is describing about truth.

steps.title: Truth splits into flocks and walks away
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of רב's study hall read נעדרת as coming from עדרים, flocks. Truth breaks into groups and walks off.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of רב's study hall said: It teaches that truth becomes many flocks, and it goes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of רב's study hall explain the word נעדרת by linking it to עדרים, which means flocks. Truth breaks into separate groups and wanders off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They hear the word עדר (a flock) inside נעדרת. The picture is of truth being split into scattered groups that walk away. Truth does not just shrink; it falls apart and leaves.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of רב's study hall

phrases.english: The scholars of Rav's study hall said:
This teaches that it becomes flocks upon flocks
phrases.notes: This is wordplay: נֶעְדֶּרֶת sounds like עֲדָרִים, which means flocks.

phrases.english: and walks away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נעדרת comes from עדרים: truth breaks into scattered flocks and goes away.

steps.title: What does 'he who turns from evil is made a fool' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second half of the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and he who turns away from evil is made a fool of' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the second half of the פסוק. This sets up the next explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning away from evil is a good thing, so it is strange that such a person would be called a fool. The גמרא wants to know who is mocking him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who turns away from evil

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'And he who turns away from evil is made a fool of'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the פסוק to the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a person who avoids evil would be called משתולל.

steps.title: People call the honest man crazy
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of רבי שילא's study hall explain that whoever stays away from evil will be seen as crazy by other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of רבי שילא's study hall said: Anyone who turns away from evil is treated as crazy by people.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of רבי שילא's study hall explain that in that generation, a person who avoids evil will be thought of as crazy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is not actually foolish. Other people label him that way. When dishonesty is normal, the honest person looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of רבי שילא's study hall

steps.whatToRemember: Before משיח, truth falls apart and walks away, and the person who stays away from evil is called crazy.

phrases.english: The scholars of Rabbi Sheila's study hall said:
Anyone who turns away from evil
is considered crazy by people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 10 and finishes the explanation of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משתולל means that people treat the one who avoids evil as crazy.

steps.title: רבא hears about a town called Truth
steps.stepSummary: רבא thought there was no truth anywhere in the world. Then the very honest רב טבות told him about a town called קושטא, where no one lied and no one died before their time. He married there and had two sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first I thought there was no truth in the world. Then a certain Sage told me something, and his name was רב טבות (some say רב טביומי). He was so honest that he would not change his words even for all the treasures of the world. He told me: Once I came to a place called 'Truth.' The people there never changed their words, and no one there died before his time. I married a woman from there and had two sons with her.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is truth going missing, רבא tells a story. A totally honest Sage told him about a town where everyone always told the truth and no one died young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא first believed truth was gone completely. The story shows that a place of truth did exist. The fact that nobody there died before his time sets up what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: Truth (Aramaic); also the name of the town
He would not change his word (would not lie)

phrases.english: Rava said:
At first I would say
there is no truth in the world.
A certain one of the Sages said to me,
and Rav Tavut was his name,
and some say Rav Tavyomei was his name,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי הֲווֹ יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ כֹּל חֲלָלֵי דְּעָלְמָא
phrases.english: who, if they would give him all the riches of the world,
phrases.notes: Literally 'all the empty spaces of the world.' It means everything in the whole world.

phrases.english: would not change his word.
One time I happened to come to a certain place,
phrases.notes: Now רב טבות is talking. The 'I' here is him, not רבא.

phrases.english: and Truth was its name,
and they would not change their words,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה מָיֵית אִינִישׁ מֵהָתָם בְּלָא זִימְנֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and no person from there would die before his time.
I married a woman from among them,
and I had two sons from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the theme of truth going missing from Step 7 and opens a story about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was once a place of complete truth, where honesty kept people alive.

steps.title: One white lie, and the cost
steps.stepSummary: רב טבות told a neighbor that his wife was not home, because he felt it was not polite to say she was washing her hair. His two sons died. The townspeople begged him to leave so he would not bring early death on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day his wife was sitting and washing her hair. Her neighbor came and knocked on the door. He thought: it is not proper to say what she is doing. He said to the neighbor: She is not here. His two sons died. The people of the place came to him and asked: What is this? He told them: This is what happened. They said to him: Please leave our place, and do not bring death on these people.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רב טבות tells one small lie to protect his wife's privacy. Right away his sons die, and the town asks him to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a well-meant lie broke the truth that protected this town. The townspeople knew that early death came from changing one's words. That is why they sent him away.
steps.confusionAlert: Some verbs switch between 'I' and 'he.' It is the same person, רב טבות, throughout. Sometimes he is telling it himself, and sometimes רבא is retelling it.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a polite white lie destroyed what protected the town of Truth. This shows how rare and fragile truth is.

phrases.english: One day his wife was sitting
and washing her head.
Her neighbor came and knocked on the door.
I thought: it is not proper manners.
phrases.notes: He felt it was not polite to tell the neighbor that his wife was washing.

phrases.english: I said to her: She is not here.
His two sons died.
The people of the place came before him,
they said to him: What is this?
He said to them: This is what happened.
They said to him: Please,
leave our place

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא תְּגָרֵי בְּהוּ מוֹתָנָא בְּהָנָךְ אִינָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: and do not stir up death against these people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes רבא's story from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the town of Truth, even a small lie brought early death, so the liar had to leave.

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: no respect in the generation of משיח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the signs of משיח. רבי נהוראי's ברייתא says that in the generation of בן דוד, the young will shame the old, family respect will break down, and the generation will act like a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נהוראי says, in the generation when בן דוד comes, young people will shame old people, and old people will stand up for young people. A daughter will rise against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. The face of the generation will be like the face of a dog, and a son will not be ashamed in front of his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The story is finished, and the גמרא returns to describing the generation before משיח. רבי נהוראי gives another ברייתא with his own list of signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's list in Step 6 focused on Torah and truth. רבי נהוראי's list focuses on lost respect: between young and old, and inside families. The usual order of honor is turned upside down.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Nehorai says,
In the generation in which the son of David comes,
youths will shame the elders,
phrases.notes: Literally 'whiten the faces,' like a face going pale from embarrassment.

phrases.english: and elders will stand up before youths,
and a daughter rises against her mother,
and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
and the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog,
and a son will not be ashamed before his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's story and goes back to the signs of the generation before משיח, adding to רבי יהודה's list from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation of בן דוד will lose all respect between young and old and inside the family.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's list of signs before משיח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נחמיה: in the generation of בן דוד there will be arrogance, high prices, expensive wine despite good harvests, a whole kingdom turned to heresy, and no one accepting rebuke.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נחמיה says, in the generation when the son of David comes, arrogance will grow, high prices will twist people, the vine will give its fruit yet wine will be expensive, the whole kingdom will turn to heresy, and there will be no rebuke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with a list of signs for the generation of משיח, this time from רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי נהוראי's list in the last step, this one describes a world where society breaks down. The new details are economic hardship and the whole ruling kingdom turning to heresy, with nobody willing to hear criticism.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuke, correcting someone who does wrong

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Nechemya says,
the generation in which the son of David comes,
arrogance will increase,
and high prices will make people crooked,
phrases.notes: Literally 'the expensiveness will twist.'

phrases.english: and the vine will give its fruit, yet wine will be expensive,
and the whole kingdom will be turned to heresy,
and there will be no rebuke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא listing signs of the generation of בן דוד, parallel to רבי נהוראי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation of משיח will have arrogance, harsh prices, a kingdom turned to heresy, and no one accepting rebuke.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this ברייתא backs up רבי יצחק, who said בן דוד will not come until the whole kingdom turns to heresy.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יצחק, because רבי יצחק said: the son of David will not come until the whole kingdom turns to heresy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one line in רבי נחמיה's ברייתא matches what an אמורא, רבי יצחק, said on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's statement could have looked like his private opinion. Now we see an older ברייתא saying the same thing, so his view has support.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yitzchak,
for Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The son of David does not come
until the whole kingdom turns to heresy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the line 'the whole kingdom will turn to heresy' from step 15 as support for רבי יצחק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's statement that משיח comes only after the whole kingdom turns to heresy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נחמיה's ברייתא, which has the same line.

steps.title: רבא gives the פסוק behind רבי יצחק's idea
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks which פסוק teaches this and answers with the פסוק about צרעת: when it has all turned white, the person is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the פסוק? 'It has all turned white; he is pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finds a source in the תורה for the idea that the redemption comes only when the whole kingdom turns bad.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the laws of צרעת, a small white patch makes a person impure, but if the white covers his whole body he is pure. In the same way, once everything has 'turned' completely, the turnaround to redemption comes.
steps.confusionAlert: Turning to heresy is not a good thing in itself. The point is only that the redemption comes when things reach total bottom, just like the fully white person.

phrases.english: Rava said: What is the verse?
"It has all turned white; he is pure."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:13. About צרעת: once the whole skin has turned white, the person is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for רבי יצחק's statement in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that משיח comes once everything has turned bad is learned from the צרעת law that a fully white person is pure.

steps.title: A ברייתא: משיח comes when informers increase
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes a פסוק in דברים about ה׳ judging His people when their strength is gone, and learns that בן דוד will not come until informers increase.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'For ה׳ will judge His people... when He sees that their strength is gone, and none is shut up or left.' The son of David will not come until informers increase.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that uses a פסוק to describe the low point that must come before משיח. The first explanation is that informers will become common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'their strength is gone' (אזלת יד) describe the Jewish people at their weakest. The first reading says the weakness comes from informers who hand Jews over to the government.

keyTerms.meaning: Informers who betray Jews to the authorities

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"For the Lord will judge His people, etc.
phrases.notes: דברים 32:36. The word in square brackets, וְגוֹ׳ ('etc.'), is part of the corrected wording. It just means the פסוק continues.

phrases.english: when He sees that their strength is gone
and there is none shut up or left."
The son of David does not come
until informers increase.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כִּי יָדִין ה׳ עַמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on the same theme, built on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'their strength is gone' we learn משיח will not come until informers increase.

steps.title: Other readings: fewer students, no money left
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives two more explanations: משיח will not come until Torah students become few, or until even the smallest coin is gone from people's pockets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: until the students become few. Another explanation: until the פרוטה is gone from the pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers other ways to read 'their strength is gone': spiritual weakness (fewer students) or financial weakness (no money).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each דבר אחר takes the same words of the פסוק and finds a different kind of weakness in them. They do not argue about the basic idea, only about which kind of 'strength' will run out.

phrases.english: Another explanation: until the students become few.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַד שֶׁתִּכְלֶה פְּרוּטָה מִן הַכִּיס.
phrases.english: Another explanation: until the perutah is gone from the pocket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other readings of the same פסוק from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Their strength is gone' can also mean fewer Torah students, or total poverty.

steps.title: Last reading: when people give up hope
steps.stepSummary: The final explanation: משיח will not come until people give up on the redemption, learned from 'none is shut up or left,' as if Israel has no one to support or help them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: until they despair of the redemption, as it says, 'and none is shut up or left.' It is as if Israel has no supporter and no helper.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its last reading, this time from the second half of the פסוק: משיח comes when people have given up hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the weakness is in people's hope itself. 'None is shut up or left' is read as a feeling that nobody at all is there to help Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: As if it could be said

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads one פסוק four ways. Each describes a different low point (informers, few students, poverty, despair) that comes before משיח.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּתְיָיאֲשׁוּ מִן הַגְּאוּלָּה,
phrases.english: Another explanation: until they despair of the redemption,
as it says: "And none is shut up or left"
as if there is no supporter
and helper for Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּתְיָיאֲשׁוּ מִן הַגְּאוּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the alternative readings, now drawn from the end of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיח will come when people have given up hope of redemption.

steps.title: רבי זירא: do not push משיח away by calculating
steps.stepSummary: Connected to the idea of despair, רבי זירא would beg scholars who were calculating when משיח would come to stop, because משיח, like a lost item and a scorpion, comes when no one is thinking about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבי זירא. When he found Rabbis busy with it, he told them: Please, I beg you, do not push it away. For we learned: three things come when the mind is distracted: משיח, a found object, and a scorpion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי זירא acted on the idea from the last step. He told people who were busy figuring out משיח's date to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משיח comes when people are not expecting him, then calculating and watching for him actually holds him back. רבי זירא backs this up with a ברייתא listing three things that come by surprise.

keyTerms.meaning: When the mind is turned away, not paying attention

phrases.english: Like that of Rabbi Zeira:
when he would find Rabbis
who were busy with it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means figuring out when משיח will come.

phrases.english: he said to them: Please,
I ask of you, do not push it far away,
for we learned: Three things come when the mind is distracted,
and these are they: Messiah, a found object, and a scorpion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 20: משיח comes when people are not expecting him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calculating משיח's arrival pushes it away, since משיח comes unexpectedly.

steps.title: רב קטינא: the world lasts 6,000 years, one in ruins
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says the world exists for six thousand years and then lies in ruins for one thousand, based on the פסוק 'ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: The world exists for six thousand years, and for one thousand it is destroyed, as it says: 'And ה׳ alone will be exalted on that day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic about the timeline of the world. רב קטינא gives the length of the world and how long it will be destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'That day' is treated as one 'day' of ה׳, which is a thousand years. During that time only ה׳ is exalted, meaning the world as we know it is gone.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
Six thousand years the world exists,
and for one it is in ruins,
phrases.notes: 'One' means one thousand years.

phrases.english: as it says: "And the Lord alone will be exalted on that day."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 2:11. A 'day' of ה׳ is taken as a thousand years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: שֵׁית אַלְפֵי שְׁנֵי הָוֵי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the timeline of the world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world lasts 6,000 years and then lies in ruins for 1,000.

steps.title: אביי: the world will be in ruins for two thousand years
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees and says the world will be in ruins for two thousand years, based on the פסוק 'After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For two thousand it is destroyed, as it says: 'He will revive us after two days; on the third day He will raise us up, and we will live before Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues with רב קטינא about how long the ruin lasts. He says two thousand years, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses a פסוק in הושע that speaks of two 'days' before revival. Each 'day' is a thousand years, so the ruin lasts two thousand years before the 'third day' of new life.

keyTerms.meaning: He will bring us back to life

steps.whatToRemember: רב קטינא says the world is in ruins for 1,000 years; אביי says 2,000. Each brings a פסוק, and each 'day' of ה׳ means a thousand years.

phrases.english: Abaye said: For two it is in ruins,
as it says: "He will revive us after two days;
phrases.notes: הושע 6:2.

phrases.english: on the third day He will raise us up,
and we will live before Him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב קטינא in step 22 about how long the world is in ruins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world will be in ruins for two thousand years, learned from 'after two days He will revive us.'

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב קטינא: the world rests like שמיטה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up רב קטינא: just as שמיטה releases one year out of seven, the world 'rests' for one thousand years out of every seven thousand. It brings three פסוקים as sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב קטינא: Just as the שמיטה year releases one year out of every seven, so too the world rests for one thousand years out of every seven thousand. As it says: 'And ה' alone will be exalted on that day.' And it says: 'A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day,' meaning a 'day' that is entirely Shabbat. And it says: 'For a thousand years in Your eyes are like yesterday when it has passed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב קטינא's view from step 22: six thousand years of the world, then one thousand years of ruin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a new reason: the pattern of שמיטה. Six years of working the land and then one year of rest match six thousand years of the world and then one thousand years of 'rest.' The third פסוק is the key link: it shows that one 'day' for ה׳ equals a thousand years, so 'a day that is all Shabbat' means a thousand-year Shabbat.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him (support for an אמורא)
The seventh year, the שמיטה year
Releases / lets rest (from the word שמיטה)
A day that is entirely Shabbat

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'day' here does not mean 24 hours. The whole proof depends on the third פסוק, which says one of ה׳'s 'days' is a thousand years.
steps.whyThisMatters: In the dispute between רב קטינא (1,000 years of ruin) and אביי (2,000 years), this ברייתא sides with רב קטינא through the seven-part שמיטה pattern.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רב קטינא:
Just as the seventh (שמיטה) year releases
one year out of every seven years,
so too the world rests
one thousand years out of every seven thousand years,
as it says: 'And ה' alone will be exalted on that day,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 2:11. This is the same פסוק רב קטינא used in step 22.

phrases.english: and it says: 'A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day' —
phrases.notes: תהלים 92:1

phrases.english: a day that is entirely Shabbat.
And it says: 'For a thousand years in Your eyes
are like yesterday once it has passed.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's disagreement in step 23, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב קטינא's view from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב קטינא's view that the world exists for six thousand years and is in ruins for one thousand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that compares the world to the שמיטה cycle and uses ישעיהו 2:11, תהלים 92:1 and תהלים 90:4.

steps.title: תנא דבי אליהו: six thousand years in three periods
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו teaches that the world lasts six thousand years, divided into two thousand years of chaos, two thousand of Torah, and two thousand of the days of משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of אליהו taught: The world exists for six thousand years. Two thousand years are chaos, two thousand years are Torah, and two thousand years are the days of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from תנא דבי אליהו that divides the six thousand years of the world into three equal periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the idea of six thousand years of the world from the previous steps, and now explains what happens inside those years. It splits them into three blocks of two thousand: a time of chaos, a time of Torah, and a time when משיח can come.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of אליהו taught (a source of teachings linked to אליהו הנביא)

steps.whatToRemember: The world's six thousand years are divided into three parts of two thousand years each: תוהו, תורה, and ימות המשיח.

phrases.english: The school of אליהו taught:
The world exists for six thousand years,
two thousand years of chaos,
two thousand years of Torah,
two thousand years of the days of משיח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about the seventh thousand years, the גמרא describes how the first six thousand years are divided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six thousand years of the world are divided into three periods: two thousand of chaos, two thousand of Torah, and two thousand of the days of משיח.
